The private data source connect (PDC) feature lets you establish a secure connection between Grafana Cloud and a PostgreSQL database on a private network.

Grafana Cloud can't reach databases on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or private IP ranges (`10.x`, `172.16.x`, `192.168.x`) directly. If your database isn't publicly accessible, PDC creates a secure tunnel so the connection can succeed.
**Recommendation:** We recommend that you create a private connection whenever you connect Grafana Cloud to an external data source.

In the **Private data source connect** field, select the name of a PDC agent.

**Note:** For the test connection to succeed, you must select a PDC agent that's running. Skip this step if your database is publicly accessible.

Click **Save & test**.

When successful, you'll see the message: `Database Connection OK`. Grafana also auto-detects your PostgreSQL server version on save.
In the next milestone, you'll verify that your PostgreSQL data appears correctly in Grafana Cloud.

---

### Troubleshooting

Explore the following troubleshooting topics if you need help:

- [Failed to connect to PostgreSQL](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/postgres/troubleshooting/#failed-to-connect-to-postgresql)
- [Grafana Cloud can't reach a private database](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/postgres/troubleshooting/#grafana-cloud-cant-reach-a-private-database)
- [Password authentication failed](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/postgres/troubleshooting/#password-authentication-failed)
